text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:

- Debate over cabinet reshuffle continues. CSU won't let go of proposal floated by Finance Minister Theo Waigel. But debate over whether to abolition draft for German army fades as key FDP leaders speak out in favour of maintaining induction.
- Former foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher opposed to cuts in support for eastern Germany, criticises finance ministry.

- Food concern Thomy is target of extortionist. Police say extortionists have threatened to put poisoned food in 37 supermarkets in 14 cities, including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne and Frankfurt.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl calls building of Berlin Wall 36 years ago on Wednesday a reminder for all Germans to work hard to maintain democratic values.
- Shickedanz will become second largest shareholder in Karstadt with more than 20 percent. Cartel office to examine proposed acquisition.
- German car importers expect busy year in 1998. Because of strong demand for imports in eastern Germany, where every second car is an import, car importers are hopeful for a big year in 1998.
- Inflation heats up because of increase in fees and taxes.
- Deutsche Telekom wants to beef up its position in Italy. It is considered possible the company will tender an offer along with Enel on the on the bourse for Olivetti.
- Karstadt shares rise sharply after Schickendanz group says it will take big stake in group.
- CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble warns against debate over cabinet reshuffle. Says government has to concnetrate on breakthrough against SPD blockade tactics in Bundesrat.
- German car club sees trend towards economically friendly cars.
- German inflation rises to highest level since 1995
